title: A Light in the Bog
summary: You drift into Lamplight Hollow on a raft, your little lantern still burning.

intro.speaker: Warden Hollis
intro.text: A light! On a raft! Are you real?

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: I think so. Where am I?

intro.speaker: Warden Hollis
intro.text: Lamplight Hollow. What's left of it. Come in, quick — well, not quick. Come in.

outro.speaker: Warden Hollis
outro.text: Your wick is still burning. Nobody's is, any more.

outro.speaker: Warden Hollis
outro.text: You're a Wickbearer. We've been waiting for one.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: What do I do?

outro.speaker: Warden Hollis
outro.text: Carry the light. Share it when you can. We'll start small.

title: Bedtime for Bones
summary: The Rattlebones have climbed out of the Drowned Graves. Send them home.

intro.speaker: Warden Hollis
intro.text: The graveyard slid into the bog. The bones woke up.

intro.speaker: Warden Hollis
intro.text: They're not wicked. Just lost. Your light will remind them.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: And the floating lamps?

intro.speaker: Warden Hollis
intro.text: Grab any you see. We tie them down with string.

outro.speaker: Warden Hollis
outro.text: Five lamps! Mother Mabble will cry into the soup.

outro.speaker: Warden Hollis
outro.text: And the Rattlers went home to bed. Did you hear them say thank you?

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: Very quietly. Yes.

title: Flicker's Cousin
summary: A tiny wisp is lost in the graves. Bring her home safely.

intro.speaker: Flicker
intro.text: My cousin Glim went into the graves. I'm not worried! *flicker*

intro.speaker: Flicker
intro.text: Okay, I'm very worried.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: I'll find her.

outro.speaker: Glim
outro.text: Thank you! It was so dark I forgot which way was up.

outro.speaker: Flicker
outro.text: You brought her back! I'll open the waypoint to the crypts for you.

outro.speaker: Flicker
outro.text: Oh, and— Glim said she saw a grey man in a grey hat. Just standing. Watching the bell tower.

twist: First glimpse of the Grey Guest.

title: Pocket Nineteen
summary: A Magpie Imp stole the crypt key from Pocket Polly. Catch it!

intro.speaker: Pocket Polly
intro.text: Pocket nineteen! It had the crypt key! A Magpie Imp took it!

intro.speaker: Pocket Polly
intro.text: It's somewhere in Bellcrypt Halls. Giggling. They always giggle.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: How do I catch it?

intro.speaker: Pocket Polly
intro.text: Be faster than it. Or smarter. Faster's easier.

outro.speaker: Pocket Polly
outro.text: The key! And a pile of gold! That imp was busy.

outro.speaker: Pocket Polly
outro.text: Keep the gold. The imp won't miss it. Much.

outro.speaker: Pocket Polly
outro.text: The key opens the Sunken Nave. That's where the bell sound comes from.

title: The Yawning Nave
summary: Villagers are asleep in the Sunken Nave. Wake them with the little bells.

objectives.text: Ring the three hand-bells in order

intro.speaker: Sleepy villager
intro.text: Zzz… come home… zzz…

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: They're all asleep. Standing up.

intro.speaker: Grandmother Purl
intro.text: (from far away) Little light! Ring the small bells: low, middle, high. That's the waking song.

outro.speaker: Sleepy villager
outro.text: Huh? Where's my hat? Where's my HOUSE?

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: Home is that way. Follow the lamps.

outro.speaker: Sleepy villager
outro.text: The big bell kept ringing. It sounded… so worried.

twist: The sleeping curse comes from the bell. The bell is worried, not wicked.

title: Who Rings the Bell?
summary: Grandmother Purl knows that bell. She knows who rang it.

objectives.text: Get the belfry gate opened by Big Bran

intro.speaker: Grandmother Purl
intro.text: That bell belongs to Tolly Clapperton. Sixty years he rang it.

intro.speaker: Grandmother Purl
intro.text: 'Come home, come home, the dark is coming.'

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Where is he now?

intro.speaker: Grandmother Purl
intro.text: Nobody's seen him since the Lantern went out. Nobody's looked.

outro.speaker: Big Bran
outro.text: The belfry gate's rusted shut. Hammer Gerald can fix that.

outro.speaker: Big Bran
outro.text: CLANG. There. Oh no. Was that a moth?

outro.speaker: Grandmother Purl
outro.text: Be gentle with him, little light. He was only trying to call us home.

twist: The boss is someone the village loved.

title: Belfry of the Drowned
summary: Climb the sunken tower. Stop the bell. Bring Tolly home.

objectives.text: Climb the Belfry of the Drowned

intro.speaker: The Sunken Bellringer
intro.text: DONG. Come home… come home…

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Tolly! Everyone's home! You can stop!

intro.speaker: The Sunken Bellringer
intro.text: The dark is coming… DONG…

outro.speaker: Tolly
outro.text: Oh. Did everyone get home?

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: They did. You can rest now.

outro.speaker: Tolly
outro.text: Then one more ring. The good one.

outro.speaker: Tolly
outro.text: DING! Morning bell!

title: The Morning Bell
summary: The lamps drift down. Tolly has something to tell you.

intro.speaker: Warden Hollis
intro.text: The lamps came down on their own! Every one!

intro.speaker: Tolly
intro.text: And I'm ringing the town bell now. When you come home. Only then.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Tolly, what happened that night?

outro.speaker: Tolly
outro.text: A grey man knocked on my door. He asked to sit down. Just for a minute.

outro.speaker: Tolly
outro.text: I said I was busy. I had a bell to ring.

outro.speaker: Tolly
outro.text: He looked so tired. Then he walked into the woods.

outro.speaker: Warden Hollis
outro.text: Whisperwood. You'll follow him?

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: I'll follow him.

twist: The Grey Guest wasn't attacking. He was asking for help.

title: Rope Bridges
summary: Owlstead hangs in the trees. Someone up there jumps at every whisper.

intro.speaker: Ranger Sorrel
intro.text: AH! Oh. A person. Sorry. The trees keep whispering.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: What are they saying?

intro.speaker: Ranger Sorrel
intro.text: Rumours. About you, now. Something about your boots.

outro.speaker: Ranger Sorrel
outro.text: A grey man? Yes. He walked through a while ago.

outro.speaker: Ranger Sorrel
outro.text: He didn't have a shadow. Nobody here does, any more.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: Look — neither do I.

twist: Your own shadow is gone the moment you enter Whisperwood.

title: What the Birches Say
summary: The Gossiping Birches know where the shadows went. Only one of them tells the truth.

intro.speaker: Birch
intro.text: Psst. The shadows went north.

intro.speaker: Other birch
intro.text: Don't listen. They went south.

intro.speaker: Third birch
intro.text: I'm the only one who never lies. Also, I love your boots.

outro.speaker: Honest birch
outro.text: Fine. Fine! Mother Bark took them. For safekeeping, she says.

outro.speaker: Honest birch
outro.text: And your boots are… okay.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: Thanks. I think.

title: Old Hoot's Questions
summary: The oldest owl answers everything with a question. Somehow, that helps.

intro.speaker: Old Hoot
intro.text: Why would a tree take shadows? What is a shadow without light?

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Nothing?

intro.speaker: Old Hoot
intro.text: Then what happens to shadows when the light goes out?

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: …They fade away. Oh.

outro.speaker: Old Hoot
outro.text: So is Mother Bark stealing? Or saving?

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: Saving. She's saving them.

outro.speaker: Old Hoot
outro.text: Who taught you to think like that? Was it me? Hoo.

twist: Mother Bark is protecting the shadows, not stealing them.

title: Doughnut Is Missing
summary: Juniper's owlet flew into Puffcap Hollow. Owlets and spores do not mix.

objectives.text: Ask Professor Puffcap about the spores

intro.speaker: Juniper
intro.text: Doughnut flew off! Hoo! Sorry. She's only small.

intro.speaker: Juniper
intro.text: She'll follow a light. Please be her light.

outro.speaker: Juniper
outro.text: DOUGHNUT! Hoo hoo hoo! Sorry. Happy hoots.

outro.speaker: Professor Puffcap
outro.text: You walked through my Hollow and didn't sneeze once? Impressive. *puff*

outro.speaker: Professor Puffcap
outro.text: Come by the lab. I'll show you some alchemy. It helps with the Owl Towers.

title: The Owl Towers
summary: Owlcrows guard the way to the Pantry. They'll let you pass — if you answer their riddle.

intro.speaker: Owlcrow
intro.text: Riddle! What gets bigger the more you take away?

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Um.

intro.speaker: Owlcrow
intro.text: Take your time. We turn our heads all the way round while we wait.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: A hole! The answer is a hole.

outro.speaker: Owlcrow
outro.text: Correct! You may pass. Also, we will be watching. We are always watching.

outro.speaker: Owlcrow
outro.text: (kindly) Go gently with the old tree.

title: The Shadow Pantry
summary: Thousands of jars. Thousands of shadows. One very old tree.

intro.speaker: Mother Bark
intro.text: Thief! Shadow-snatcher! You'll not have my little darks!

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: I don't want to take them. I want to take them home.

intro.speaker: Mother Bark
intro.text: Home? There IS no home for them! No light, no shadow!

outro.speaker: Mother Bark
outro.text: …Is that MY shadow? On the ground?

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: My light made it.

outro.speaker: Mother Bark
outro.text: Ha! Haha! Oh, it's been a year!

outro.speaker: Mother Bark
outro.text: Open the jars, little darks. Go home.

title: The Empty Jar
summary: Every jar is open. All but one — and that one was always empty.

intro.speaker: Mother Bark
intro.text: There's one jar I never filled. See the label?

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: 'Shadow of a tall grey stranger.' It's empty.

intro.speaker: Mother Bark
intro.text: He had no shadow to catch. His light was all the way out. Inside.

outro.speaker: Mother Bark
outro.text: Here. An acorn, too. Plant it someday. Somebody in there needs a long nap.

outro.speaker: Ranger Sorrel
outro.text: He went under the mountain, the birds say. To the Echo Mines.

outro.speaker: Ranger Sorrel
outro.text: Wickbearer? Your shadow's back. It's following you. It likes you.

twist: The Grey Guest's own light is completely out — he is Snuffed too.

title: Going Down
summary: Clinkerton sits on a giant lift. It creaks. Everything creaks.

intro.speaker: Lou Lever
intro.text: Going down! Floor one: Clinkerton! Floor two: also Clinkerton!

intro.speaker: Foreman Hilda
intro.text: A Wickbearer. Good. I have a list.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: A list of what?

outro.speaker: Foreman Hilda
outro.text: Why we dig. It's blank. We forgot.

outro.speaker: Foreman Hilda
outro.text: My crew became Diglings. They dig and dig and don't know why.

outro.speaker: Foreman Hilda
outro.text: And the mountain… copies us. Wrong way round.

title: Scraps of a Song
summary: The Saltwhistle Shafts whistle a tune. Pieces of it are written on old helmets.

intro.speaker: Foreman Hilda
intro.text: There used to be a song. Every crew had it on their helmets.

intro.speaker: Foreman Hilda
intro.text: Find the helmets. Find the words.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: 'Dig deep.' 'Bring the shine.' 'The mountain sings.'

outro.speaker: Foreman Hilda
outro.text: That's it! Some of it. It's in the wrong order, though.

outro.speaker: Echo Annie
outro.text: Order. Order.

title: Lenny's Lamp
summary: A lamp ghost floats through the Glittering Gallery, calling for his miner.

intro.speaker: Lenny
intro.text: Have you seen my miner? Big boots. Bad jokes. I was his lamp.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: We'll find him together.

intro.speaker: Lenny
intro.text: Mind the spiders. If the clinking stops, look up.

outro.speaker: Lenny
outro.text: BARNABY! It's me! Your lamp!

outro.speaker: Barnaby
outro.text: LENNY! HA HA HA! Sorry! Lift's fine!

outro.speaker: Barnaby
outro.text: I remember now. I used to sing while you glowed. Something about… digging bright?

twist: Barnaby the innkeeper was a miner. He remembers a line.

title: The Cart With Teeth
summary: Something with teeth rattles on the Rattletrack Rails. It's guarding something.

intro.speaker: Pickett
intro.text: Cart six never came back. There's a cart with TEETH out there instead.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Maybe it ate cart six.

intro.speaker: Pickett
intro.text: Don't say that. Cart six is adventurous, not edible.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: The toothy cart was guarding a little Digling. Asleep in cart six.

outro.speaker: Pickett
outro.text: Keeping him safe? Aw. Even the teeth were kind.

outro.speaker: Pickett
outro.text: Cart six, you hero.

twist: The monster was protecting someone smaller.

title: Dig Deep, Dig Bright
summary: Put the song back together. The mountain is listening.

objectives.text: Put the song lines in order

intro.speaker: Echo Annie
intro.text: The song goes in a circle, dearie. Circle.

intro.speaker: Echo Annie
intro.text: Start deep. End singing. Singing.

outro.speaker: Dorra
outro.text: DIG DEEP, DIG BRIGHT, BRING THE SHINE TO LIGHT!

outro.speaker: Dorra
outro.text: DIG SLOW, DIG TRUE, THE MOUNTAIN SINGS FOR YOU!

outro.speaker: The mountain
outro.text: …THGIL OT ENIHS…

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: It's singing back. Backwards. It wants more.

title: The Mouth of the Mountain
summary: A cave so big it has weather. It copies everything. Give it something good to copy.

objectives.text: Enter the Mouth of the Mountain

intro.speaker: The Great Echo
intro.text: …OLLEH? OLLEH?

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Hello!

intro.speaker: The Great Echo
intro.text: !OLLEH! !OLLEH!

outro.speaker: The miners
outro.text: Dig deep, dig bright…

outro.speaker: The Great Echo
outro.text: …BRING THE SHINE TO LIGHT.

outro.speaker: The Great Echo
outro.text: (softly) Thank you. It was so quiet. I copied anything.

outro.speaker: The Great Echo
outro.text: I even copied him. The grey one.

title: What the Echo Heard
summary: The mountain remembers everything it ever heard. Including the Grey Guest.

objectives.text: Get the Echo Crystal set by Opaline

intro.speaker: The Great Echo
intro.text: He walked through. He said one thing. I kept it.

intro.speaker: The Great Echo
intro.text: (in a grey, tired voice) 'I'm so tired. Nobody ever asks who keeps it lit.'

outro.speaker: Opaline
outro.text: The Echo gave you a crystal? Hold still. *polish* Now it'll keep his words safe.

outro.speaker: Foreman Hilda
outro.text: Keeps it lit? Keeps WHAT lit?

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: The Lantern. I think he was its keeper.

outro.speaker: Foreman Hilda
outro.text: The birds say he went to Rimehall. The frozen castle.

twist: The Grey Guest was the Lantern's keeper.

title: The Warm Kitchens
summary: Rimehall is frozen. Only the kitchens are warm. Everyone who stayed lives there.

intro.speaker: Nan Kettleby
intro.text: In, in, in! Kettle's on. You're blue at the edges.

intro.speaker: Chancellor Snowdrop
intro.text: Ah. You're on my list. My list of people who might help. It's short.

outro.speaker: Chancellor Snowdrop
outro.text: His Majesty froze mid-toast. Then he forgot his name.

outro.speaker: Chancellor Snowdrop
outro.text: The less he remembers, the colder the castle gets.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: Then we help him remember.

title: A Princess With a Plan
summary: The king's daughter has a plan. It involves a hare, a garden, and you.

objectives.text: Guide Sir Wobble through the gardens

intro.speaker: Princess Pip
intro.text: I'm Princess Pip. My dad is the king. He forgot my name.

intro.speaker: Princess Pip
intro.text: Sir Wobble can sniff out Dad's things. Take him to the gardens.

intro.speaker: Princess Pip
intro.text: That's a royal order. Please.

outro.speaker: Princess Pip
outro.text: Sir Wobble found something! A frozen letter. It says 'A'.

outro.speaker: Princess Pip
outro.text: It's from Dad's name. His name is on everything, and the frost broke it into bits.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: Then we find all the bits.

title: The Frosted Gardens
summary: The hedges are shaped like animals. Some of them are animals.

intro.speaker: Chancellor Snowdrop
intro.text: The gardens were His Majesty's favourite. He named every hedge.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Did the hedges have names?

intro.speaker: Chancellor Snowdrop
intro.text: All of them were called 'Hedge'. He was very tired that day.

outro.speaker: Princess Pip
outro.text: A! Now we need the rest.

outro.speaker: Chancellor Snowdrop
outro.text: Mind the Looking-Glass Gallery next. The reflections run late.

title: Mind the Third Mirror
summary: A hall of mirrors. Your reflection is late. Except in one.

intro.speaker: Mirror Butler
intro.text: Tea, sir? Madam? Hero? The tea is a trap. I am so sorry.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Then why serve it?

intro.speaker: Mirror Butler
intro.text: I forgot how to stop.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: In the third mirror, my reflection moved first. It pointed at the letter.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: …It had a little lantern drawn on its hand.

outro.speaker: Mister Ledger
outro.text: Curious. Noted. Underlined.

twist: Your reflection in the third mirror acts before you do — a hint of the Answering Mailbox mystery.

title: The Everlasting Toast
summary: Hundreds of frozen guests, cups raised. One chair is empty. It has a name card.

intro.speaker: Tumblewit
intro.text: Welcome to the longest party in history. Nobody's had cake in a year.

intro.speaker: Tumblewit
intro.text: That's the sad part. The funny part is also that.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: There's an empty seat at the king's right hand.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: The card says: 'Our Grey Guest.'

outro.speaker: Tumblewit
outro.text: He invited him in. The only one who ever did.

outro.speaker: Tumblewit
outro.text: …That's not a joke. I don't have a joke for that.

twist: The King was the only person who ever welcomed the Grey Guest.

title: Who Are You?
summary: The Throne of Frost. A king who has forgotten everything, even himself.

objectives.text: Remind the King who he is

intro.speaker: The King Who Forgot
intro.text: Who are you?

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: A Wickbearer. And you're—

intro.speaker: The King Who Forgot
intro.text: Who am I? No matter. Everyone must stay. Stay FROZEN.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: A-L-D-R-I-C. Your name is Aldric.

outro.speaker: King Aldric
outro.text: Aldric. …Aldric Warmhearth.

outro.speaker: King Aldric
outro.text: (raising his cup) — and to all of you, who stayed!

outro.speaker: Princess Pip
outro.text: DAD!

outro.speaker: King Aldric
outro.text: Pip. Pip! I remember you first.

title: To All of You, Who Stayed
summary: The castle thaws. The king remembers his last guest.

objectives.text: Have Master Quillon carve the Well-key

intro.speaker: King Aldric
intro.text: He sat at my table, the grey fellow. Said, 'Thank you for asking me in.'

intro.speaker: King Aldric
intro.text: He said his name was… no. He wouldn't say it.

intro.speaker: King Aldric
intro.text: Then he said he was going home. Down. To the Well of Hush.

outro.speaker: Master Quillon
outro.text: A key for the Well. Carved in ice. Don't let it near the kettle.

outro.speaker: King Aldric
outro.text: If you find him, tell him there's still a seat. Always.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: I'll tell him.

title: Lastlight Landing
summary: A lighthouse on the rim of the world. The last hall of the Wickwright Guild.

intro.speaker: Aunt Lumi
intro.text: Come in from the grey, love. There's a light in every window for you.

intro.speaker: Ada Brightly
intro.text: A Wickbearer. At last. Sit, sit. I'll stand. I always stand.

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: The Well of Hush is below us. Down there, down is up.

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: At the bottom is the sky. And the Lantern.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: And the Grey Guest?

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: (quietly) Yes. Him too.

title: Nobody Helps
summary: The Upside-Down Stars. The Hushlings drift. One of them wears a hat.

objectives.text: Follow Nobody to the fallen lanterns

intro.speaker: Nobody
intro.text: …  (A Hushling in a hat tips it at you.)

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: You're… not attacking?

intro.speaker: Nobody
intro.text: …  (It points. It wants you to follow.)

outro.speaker: Nobody
outro.text: …  (It shows you a pile of fallen lanterns. Dozens. All dark.)

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: (on the wind) The Guild's lanterns. Every keeper who gave up.

outro.speaker: Nobody
outro.text: …  (It picks one up. It gives it to you. It seems to be saying: not all of us are gone.)

twist: Not every Hushling is lost. Nobody wants to help.

title: The Drift of Leftovers
summary: Islands made of everything the Hush took. Including colours.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: A bog stair. A birch. A mine cart. A ballroom door.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: It's all the places I've been. Grey.

intro.speaker: Nib
intro.text: (from the Landing, by glow-mail) Shinies! Colours are the best shinies! Bring them back!

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: Bog-green. Birch-violet. Crystal-white. Frost-blue. Lantern-gold.

outro.speaker: Mother Simmer
outro.text: Pop them in the Cauldron, dearie. *burble* She'll mix them into something warm.

outro.speaker: Mother Simmer
outro.text: There. A little lantern-oil. You'll need it at the top. Or the bottom.

title: Ada's Confession
summary: The Moth Choir sings a song the Guild never wanted sung.

objectives.text: Find the last scrap of a name

intro.speaker: The Moth Choir
intro.text: *sing* One keeper climbed, and nobody came…

intro.speaker: The Moth Choir
intro.text: *sing* Night after night, and always the same…

intro.speaker: The Moth Choir
intro.text: *sing* His name was Pell, and he trimmed the flame…

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: Pell and I were apprentices. Together.

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: When the others left, I said: I'll climb up and help you tomorrow.

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: For forty years, I said tomorrow.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: He's not a monster, is he?

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: No. He's my friend. And he was so, so tired.

twist: The Grey Guest is Pell, the last Lantern keeper. Ada could have helped him.

title: The Quiet Stair
summary: A spiral stair down to the sky. No sound at all. Your footsteps glow instead.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: (Nothing. Not even your own voice.)

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: (But each step leaves a little light behind.)

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: (At the bottom, a sound: a small, tired breath.)

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: (Somebody is up there. Down there. Waiting.)

title: Every Light You Lit
summary: Before the last door, the friends you rekindled send you their light.

intro.speaker: Tolly
intro.text: (a bell, from very far away) DING! Come home, Wickbearer. When you're done.

intro.speaker: Mother Bark
intro.text: Take a shadow with you, little light. Shadows mean there's light.

intro.speaker: The Great Echo
intro.text: DIG DEEP. DIG BRIGHT.

intro.speaker: King Aldric
intro.text: To you, Wickbearer. And to him. There's still a seat.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: Four small lights. Bell, bark, song, toast.

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: (on the wind) A light shared is not a light lost, Wickbearer.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: I know. I think I finally know.

title: The Lantern Room
summary: Inside the dark World-Lantern. A small grey figure sits by the cold wick.

objectives.text: Share your light with the Grey Guest

intro.speaker: The Grey Guest
intro.text: You came all this way.

intro.speaker: The Grey Guest
intro.text: Please. Just let it stay dark.

intro.speaker: The Grey Guest
intro.text: Then nobody has to carry it.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: Nobody has to carry it alone.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: (You hold out your lantern. He holds out his. Small. Old. Cold.)

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: (The flame jumps across.)

outro.speaker: Pell
outro.text: …Oh. It's warm.

outro.speaker: Pell
outro.text: You carried it. I thought no one would.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: Pell. Your name is Pell.

twist: You don't win by striking. The last prompt is 'Share your light.'

title: Carry the Light
summary: The World-Lantern is lit — by every light you rekindled, shining up together.

intro.speaker: Pell
intro.text: Look. Down there. Up there. All those little lights.

intro.speaker: Pell
intro.text: Tolly's bell. The shadows. The miners. Aldric's hall.

intro.speaker: Pell
intro.text: They're all shining up. At the Lantern. Together.

intro.speaker: You
intro.text: It's lit.

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: Pell.

outro.speaker: Pell
outro.text: Ada. You came up the stair.

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: I'm forty years late.

outro.speaker: Pell
outro.text: You're here. That's what counts.

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: (to you) Kneel? No, don't. Just stand there. Wickwright.

outro.speaker: Aunt Lumi
outro.text: And then everyone rests. That's an order. Kettle's on.

twist: The player is named Wickwright. Night returns — with a morning at the end of it.

title: Where the Hush Went
summary: The Lantern is lit. But the Hush didn't vanish. It sank under everything.

objectives.text: Talk to Pell at the Landing

intro.speaker: Pell
intro.text: I trim the lighthouse wick once a week now. Because it's nice. Not because I must.

intro.speaker: Pell
intro.text: But the Hush went down. Under everything. Like night under morning.

intro.speaker: Pell
intro.text: It's not bad. It just needs tidying.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: It's all the places I've been. Upside down. Greyer.

outro.speaker: Pell
outro.text: (on the wind) Take your time. The Deepdark has had a long night. So have you.

title: The First Lightwell
summary: Every town's Lightwell drained into the Deepdark. Dive in and bring some light back up.

objectives.text: Ask Warden Hollis about the old well

intro.speaker: Warden Hollis
intro.text: Our Lightwell was full of light once. For a dark day.

intro.speaker: Warden Hollis
intro.text: Well. It's been a dark year. Want to fetch some?

outro.speaker: Warden Hollis
outro.text: Look at that! Proper old light!

outro.speaker: Warden Hollis
outro.text: Stop halfway next time and you'll still keep what you found. No rush. Ever.

title: Lantern Maps
summary: Mae Coalbright draws maps into the Deepdark. Each one is a little different.

intro.speaker: Mae Coalbright
intro.text: I've been making Lantern Maps. Still just learning.

intro.speaker: Mae Coalbright
intro.text: Foggy ones. Echoing ones. One's upside-down. Well. More upside-down.

outro.speaker: Mae Coalbright
outro.text: Three runs! You're better at this than me, and I've had seventy years.

outro.speaker: Mae Coalbright
outro.text: Keep going deeper, if you like. The Snuffed down there are stubborn, but they come round.

title: The Long Shadow
summary: Every shadow Mother Bark couldn't save gathered into one. It's very big. And very lonely.

intro.speaker: Mother Bark
intro.text: Some little darks were too far gone for my jars. They found each other down there.

intro.speaker: Mother Bark
intro.text: Now it's one big dark. It just wants to be near a light.

outro.speaker: The Long Shadow
outro.text: (It shrinks. And splits. Into hundreds of small, happy shadows.)

outro.speaker: Mother Bark
outro.text: There they go! Home, every one!

outro.speaker: Mother Bark
outro.text: It'll gather again, I expect. Shadows are sociable. Visit it whenever you like.

title: The Ninety-Ninth Chair
summary: The Guild hall has ninety-nine chairs. Somebody has been carving.

intro.speaker: Ada Brightly
intro.text: Ninety-nine chairs. For years, only mine was ever sat in.

intro.speaker: Ada Brightly
intro.text: Pell's been busy with a little knife. Go and look.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: One chair has my name on it.

outro.speaker: Pell
outro.text: And one has mine. Next to yours. If that's alright.

outro.speaker: Ada Brightly
outro.text: Sit. Both of you. Rule three.

title: The Last Letter
summary: At the very brightest, the Answering Mailbox has one more letter.

intro.speaker: Pell
intro.text: You're as bright as the Lantern ever was. Brighter, maybe.

intro.speaker: Pell
intro.text: There's a letter for you. It's been there a long time. It's in your handwriting.

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: 'Dear you. Your light never went out, because I lit it. From the other side.'

outro.speaker: You
outro.text: 'Carry it well. — You.'

outro.speaker: Pell
outro.text: So that's why you kept glowing. You were never alone either.

outro.speaker: Pell
outro.text: Kettle's on. Come and rest.

twist: You lit your own wick, from another turn of the story.
